root_cause.summary: th3-mcp-http.service (the real, canonical HTTP/remote MCP transport -- the actual path an external client like ChatGPT Work reaches via the documented approved reverse proxy) is a long-running Python process (Type=simple, no code hot-reload). It had been running continuously since 2026-09-01 06:07:56 EDT. Earlier in this SAME session (12:29:57 EDT), a prior, unrelated, already-committed piece of work in this session (the 'GOD_MODE_V1 FINAL GAP CLOSURE' campaign) added a new source_paths field to evolution/proposal.py's Proposal dataclass and threaded it through proposal_mod.create(). That code change was correct on disk from the moment it was written -- but the already-running th3-mcp-http.service process never picked it up, because Python does not hot-reload already-imported modules in a long-running process. Every submit_work call handled by that stale process hit a genuine, reproducible TypeError inside Proposal.__init__() (source_paths being passed by the now-newer create() logic against the still-old, in-process-cached Proposal class shape), which is exactly the failure signature independently confirmed in services/th3_mcp/logs/http_error.log ('tool_call_exception tool=submit_work err=TypeError("Proposal.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'source_paths'")'), recurring from 16:03:43 through 16:55:55 EDT -- i.e. after the code change, before any restart.
root_cause.confirmed_not_a_code_bug: Direct verification: (1) fresh Python introspection of evolution.proposal.Proposal.__init__ under the exact sys.path th3_mcp uses shows source_paths correctly present; (2) a direct call to proposal_mod.create() succeeded cleanly; (3) a direct call to tools.submit_work() (the exact real function) succeeded cleanly and created a real Proposal. All three prove the actual source code was already correct -- the defect was purely an unrestarted long-running process holding stale in-memory module state.
root_cause.secondary_finding_not_the_root_cause_but: This Claude session's own mcp__th3-studio__* tool calls do NOT go through th3-mcp-http.service at all -- they go through a separate MCP *stdio*-transport process (services/th3_mcp/server.py), confirmed to be a direct child process of this session's own Claude Code process (PID 224543, parent PID 224429 == this session's own 'claude' process), started at 11:21:44 EDT -- also before the 12:29:57 code change, and therefore also stale for the identical reason, but ENTIRELY SEPARATE from the HTTP transport ChatGPT Work actually uses. This is why an initial restart of th3-mcp-http.service appeared not to fix anything when re-tested via this session's own mcp__th3-studio__submit_work tool -- that tool call was hitting the unrelated stale stdio process the whole time, not the (already correctly restarted) HTTP service. This stdio process was NOT restarted or touched, since doing so risks this session's own live MCP connection and is unnecessary for the stated mission (the real, external, Work-facing path is the HTTP transport).
